page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom 64-core AWS Graviton processors built on the ARM64 architecture (ARMv9 Neoverse-V2). Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the instance features 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating simultaneous multithreading overhead. It is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation, alongside a 36 MB L3 cache. Storage is bundled directly as 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store, and networking is driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, delivering a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the instance's strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory subsystem. In memory bandwidth tests, the c8gd.16xlarge achieves top-tier performance across both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations. This memory efficiency translates to top-tier results in Passmark database operations and Geekbench software compilation. Multi-threaded decompression and physics simulations also rank in the top tier, while single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware-accelerated AES.

The ARM-based architecture provides high resource density and power efficiency, offering a favorable performance-to-overhead ratio for multi-threaded workloads without the premium of traditional x86 architectures. The combination of dedicated physical cores, high-speed local NVMe storage, and top-tier memory bandwidth makes this instance highly suitable for database hosting, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing. It also demonstrates strong capability in medium-to-large LLM inference text generation.
